semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: 'graph-based modeling' itself is a domain and would be semantically equivalent as it represents the same concept in some contexts.

parent_domains.justification: Modeling in a broader sense encompasses all kinds of modeling techniques, including graph-based, thus acting as a parent domain.
'Modelling' is just an alternative spelling of 'modeling,' serving the same broader interpretation.

closest_parent_domain.justification: The spelling 'modeling' is chosen here as it usually is the standard spelling in American English references for academic contexts, and it best envelops 'graph-based modeling.'

child_domains.justification: Graph-based machine learning is a specific application within graph-based modeling focused on applying machine learning techniques.
Graph-based learning is another specific subset of graph-based modeling aimed at educational and learning algorithms.
Graph generation is a subset that involves creating graphs, which can be seen as part of the larger graph-based modeling umbrella.
Graphical models refer to a type of statistical model that is represented by a graph and can be part of graph-based modeling.

closest_child_domain.justification: Within graph-based modeling, machine learning applications are a very close alignment to the concept, focused specifically on learning from graph data.

sibling_domains.justification: While focusing on theoretical aspects of graphs, it still falls under the broader category of using graphs as a tool or method.
These are specific types of graphical models and share the 'graph-based' title emphasis.
Graph reasoning involves using graphs to perform logical deductions and analysis, similar to modeling tasks.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: 'Graph reasoning' is closely tied to 'graph-based modeling,' as reasoning often forms a core part of modeling tasks using graphs.

unrelated_domains.justification: Graph classification is a smoother way of categorizing graphs, focusing on classification algorithms rather than modeling.
Graph regression concerns prediction tasks on graphs, more specific than the broad model-building aspect of graph-based modeling.
This domain focuses on processing signals on graphs, which is a different aspect than creating or learning from graph models.
This field is specifically focused on temporality in graphs rather than creating or interpreting graphical models themselves.
Dynamic graphs deal with changing graph structures, a more specific concept than just basic modeling.
Applies graph theory to biological data, rather than general modeling techniques.
